evidence.observation: RF2 instructs: 'Rename the three `model_digest` functions to names that state what each one means.' RF-R1 states: 'Moves and merges preserve CLI/API names, schemas, exit codes, messages, refusals, deterministic output bytes and digests. Any observable change needs its own decision row and owner ruling. Merely sitting in a refactor phase does not authorize it.' The decision table in section 10 (RF-D1..RF-D9) contains no row authorizing the model_digest renames, and RF-R5's shim inventory only guarantees that 'old import paths stay importable through re-exports' — module paths, not renamed symbols — so nothing requires `model_digest` and its siblings to remain importable after RF2. Completion predicate 1 (line 33) also requires pins to stay green 'unchanged except through recorded compatibility decisions', and no such recorded decision exists for the rename.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit decision row (or fold into an RF-D8-style ruling) authorizing the renames, and extend RF-R5 or RF2's criteria so each renamed function remains importable under its old name via a listed shim with a retirement trigger until RF-D5's retirement phase.
concerns.title: RF2 renames public model_digest API without a decision row or symbol-level shim

evidence.observation: RF4-C3 reads: 'the 47 private imports from `synth.boundary` into `synth.mutate` are replaced by public oracle imports.' The plan itself states at lines 15-16: 'No other audit claim was re-proved. RF0 re-measures all of them with a committed tool.' If RF0 refutes the audit's count of 47, the criterion as written cannot be satisfied (or could be vacuously gamed) because, unlike RF0-C1 ('reproduces at least the core 13-module SCC, or the record explains the difference'), RF4-C3 has no fallback binding it to the RF0 re-measured value.

concerns.recommendation: Reword RF4-C3 so the target count is the RF0-confirmed number of private `synth.boundary`→`synth.mutate` imports, with a recorded note if the audit's 47 is refuted, mirroring the escape hatch in RF0-C1.
concerns.title: RF4-C3 hard-codes the audit's unverified '47 private imports' as a pass/fail criterion

evidence.location: lines 232-233 (RF7 'Not executed in this milestone') vs line 313 (section 9 verification selection)
evidence.observation: RF7 states: 'Not executed in this milestone. The milestone close carries it as an open question naming the successor milestone.' Yet the verification-selection table lists RF7 as a row with the mandatory focused obligation 'Red-before-green per newly refused input' and starting points, the same format used for executable phases, and RF-D7's deferral is not referenced from that row.

concerns.recommendation: Mark the RF7 row in section 9 as deferred/not-executed (or drop it), so a reviewer at a later phase gate does not treat RF7 verification as a gating obligation of this milestone.
concerns.title: Deferred RF7 appears in the verification-selection table with a mandatory obligation

response.summary: Reviewed the code-refactoring milestone plan r1 against its rubric: pinning-before-move, digest-bound bytes, monkeypatch and source-scan coverage are all enforced by RF-R1..RF-R11 and per-phase criteria; sequencing, RF-D1/RF-D2/RF-D7 rulings, audit-claim caveats and stop conditions are consistently recorded. Three concerns: RF2 mandates renaming the three public model_digest functions with no decision row and no shim obligation for renamed symbols, contradicting RF-R1's own API-name preservation rule; RF4-C3 hard-codes the unverified audit count of 47 private imports as a criterion with no fallback to the RF0 re-measurement; and the deferred RF7 still appears in the verification-selection table with a mandatory obligation, contradicting its 'not executed in this milestone' status.
